example_prompt: List the payment methods available in Senegal with PayDunya and CinetPay, and how Cartflox ranks those providers.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Passed as a query parameter.

providers.description: Comma-separated provider keys (`paydunya,cinetpay`). Passed as a query parameter.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Passed as a query parameter.

method.description: Payment method vocabulary of the routing engine.

error_schema.description: Error body. `code` is present on transfer endpoints.

gotchas: This endpoint does not require an API key.

A quick check, without a decision: the methods available in the country for the given providers, and the providers ranked by estimated reliability. Without providers, every provider known to Cartflox is considered.
country is required (400 otherwise); providers is a comma-separated list (paydunya,cinetpay).

The docs disagree on the routing response: the OpenAPI types rankedProviders as {provider, score} objects, availableMethods items as {method, providers} and routing as {provider, reason, alternates, confidence}, while the Multi-gateway orchestration guide shows rankedProviders as plain strings, availableMethods items with code and name, and routing as {provider, method, reason: "best_success_rate"}. This spec follows the OpenAPI and stays draft until a live call settles it: parse these fields defensively.

Errors are an HTTP 4xx/5xx status with a JSON body { "error": "<message>" }. Transfer endpoints add a machine-readable code, and so do some other refusals (code test_mode on payment links, rate_limited on webhook resends). A 401 says Missing API key or Invalid API Key.
